findings.reason: entity.mjs:7 NAMED_RE matches any &name; and line 36 now calls decodeHTML, which in entities ^4.4.0 (package.json:49) is the legacy mode that decodes semicolon-less prefixes like &copy and &not. That makes decoded !== match[0] true at line 37, so the whole match is consumed and the partly decoded text is emitted. Before the change, strict decoding left these strings unchanged and the rule returned false.
findings.claim: Swapping decodeHTMLStrict for decodeHTML makes invalid named references that start with a legacy entity name (e.g. ©cat;, ¬it;) get partly decoded instead of staying literal, as CommonMark requires.
findings.evidence: NAMED_RE (`/^&([a-z][a-z0-9]{1,31});/i`, line 7) captures any `&name;`. The new line 36 `const decoded = decodeHTML(match[0])` uses entities ^4.4.0's legacy (non-strict) mode, which decodes semicolon-less legacy prefixes such as `&copy`, `&not` and `&amp` inside the match. As a result `decoded !== match[0]` is true, and the rule consumes the whole match and emits a text_special token with the partially decoded content. Before the change, decodeHTMLStrict left these strings unchanged, so the rule returned false and the text stayed literal.
